candidates: When reviewing any ASE I/O writer that handles a collection of images, flag every use of `images[0]` or other positional subscripting of the `images` argument. These patterns raise a `TypeError` when `images` is a generator or any other non-subscriptable iterable. The correct fix is to use the loop variable (e.g. `atoms`) for per-image data. If first-image data truly must be reused across all iterations (e.g. for file-header metadata), capture it before the loop with `image_0 = next(iter(images))` and document why. The same subscripting issue exists in: `ase/io/dmol.py`, `ase/io/findsym.py`, `ase/io/proteindatabank.py`, `ase/io/xsd.py`, `ase/io/xsf.py`, and `ase/io/xtd.py`.

Inside a `for atoms in images` loop in an ASE I/O writer, question every use of `images[0].X` even when `images` is subscriptable. Using the first image's attribute (e.g. constraints) for all loop iterations is almost certainly a logic bug; the current image's attribute (`atoms.X`) should be used instead. If always reading from the first image is intentional, add an explicit comment explaining the design rationale.

When an ASE I/O writer is updated to accept `Iterable[Atoms]` inputs (beyond the currently documented `Sequence[Atoms]`), update the type annotation for `write()` in `ase/io/formats.py` accordingly. The current annotation is `Union[Atoms, Sequence[Atoms]]`; widening it to `Union[Atoms, Iterable[Atoms]]` (or equivalent) keeps the public API contract honest and avoids misleading callers.

When inserting a standalone note line into the body of an existing function docstring, do not add extraneous blank lines around it beyond standard RST paragraph-separation rules. Match the blank-line convention of the surrounding docstring text.

In `changelog.d/` scriv RST fragments, do not leave a trailing blank line at the end of a bullet item. The bullet text should end immediately with the RST merge-request reference (e.g. `(:mr:\`XXXX\`)`) and no blank line should follow within that bullet.
